verdicts.reason: Depends on I005's rule that the selector sees only the ledger and on which objections cannot be scripted, and names I006's dependence on I005's ledger.
Attacks the specific formula s = P - 2F and the 3-claim floor, with a calculation from the card's own 4-8 claims and 40% checkable numbers.
Targets I005's 40% checkable-claims assumption and uses I004 and I003 claims as counterexamples, so it cannot be pasted onto another idea unchanged.
Examines whether the FActScore and CRITIC citations (arXiv numbers given) actually support I005's claim decomposition, which is specific to this card.
Concerns I005's specific rule that a novelty claim FAILs on a falsified library hit, and the library-schema assumption behind it.
Targets I005's one-brief on/off design and the circularity between its falsified-claim-rate metric and the ledger arm's own filter.
Depends on I004's mechanism of collecting loss reasons per finalist and computes expected losses for a leader versus the bottom item.
Ties judge-bias risk to I004's use of LLM judge reasons plus an LLM acceptance verifier, and to which biases its length control and both-order gate address.
Computes the 0.25 false-acceptance probability from I004's specific both-orders gate and the claim that it makes the loop monotone.
Hinges on I004's specific +/-5% token budget and the resulting ~17-token change for a 350-token card.
Quotes I006's dependency on Card 0's ledger and its 'rows = ledger.where(...)' spec, which is unique to this idea.
Depends on I006's rule that every non-PASS claim is struck after iteration 3 and on INCONCLUSIVE semantics inherited from I005.
Points out the circularity between I006's strike-on-fail rule and its falsified-claim-rate outcome measure.
Contrasts Voyager's environment-verified skills with I006's templates that are only executed, and cites its contested-rate > 0.3 filter.
Uses I003's offline-replay test and the fact that only delivered top-3 have panel ratings, which is specific to its selection-rule change.
Targets I003's fixed tau = 0.5 x pooled SD and derives the implied 0.2 within-cluster correlation.
Argues that I003's B=2000 bootstrap plus expected-max criterion favours high-variance, less-compared items, with a formula for that rule.
Depends on I003's greedy rule, whose first pick equals the top-1, so only picks 2 and 3 change, and on the card's own conceded failure modes.
Argues that I001's MATURE boundary-targeting concentrates improvement at rank 3/4 and contrasts this with LUCB and its own uniform control arm.
Computes a 0.33 false-replacement rate from I001's specific acceptance rule (3 variants, both orderings plus one incumbent comparison).
Targets I001's Round 0 with 3 comparisons per idea, 200 bootstraps and no BT prior, and contrasts I003's ridge prior.
Depends on I001's 10-brief cheapest test and on the change touching only slot 3, and contrasts I002's power calculation.
Counts I002's operator x criterion cells and warm-up records from its own 20-brief, 540-contest numbers to show the memory is inert.
Recomputes I002's 390-per-arm power figure and applies a design effect for its 30 briefs x 18 contests structure.
Argues I002 is a second-order layer on I001's mutation loop, using its stated assumption 'Card 0's contest loop exists' and the slot-3 restriction.
Uses I004's 'accept only if the revision wins both' rule for a 25% false-acceptance figure and its relative loss-reasons mechanism.
Depends on I004's requirement of a different-family verifier plus a third-family panel and its listed failure mode.
Depends on I004's +/-5% token budget with one retry and its stated assumption and failure list, and compares I001's 10% cap.
Targets I003's hand-set shared cluster shift with tau = 0.5 SD and argues it reduces to an MMR-style penalty.
Targets I003's greedy expected-max step over bootstrap samples, arguing it favours high-variance items (optimiser's curse) in slots 2-3.
